# Readable in Both Themes, Fixed from Corner to Corner

Version 1.7.4 is a fix release: warning colours are readable on light and dark cards, the card fits narrow slots, and the map, the lightbox and "show more" work from the keyboard.

## Colours and layout

- **Severity colours now follow the theme.** The fixed colours were hard to read on some cards: Minor yellow on a light card and Extreme dark pink on a dark card were nearly invisible. The card now picks a light or dark palette from the same theme detection as before (`theme_mode`, or your Home Assistant theme in auto mode), and every level reaches at least 4.5:1 contrast. On a light card you will see darker tones than before, for example a dark amber for Minor and a deeper red for Severe; on a dark card the colours are brighter, for example a light pink for Extreme. If you set `color_overrides`, your colours are kept exactly as you chose them.
- **Warnings with an unknown severity are grey.** A NINA warning with severity "Unknown" or none was drawn in the green of "no warnings". It is now a neutral grey, and the green stays reserved for the empty state.
- **The card can be made narrower.** It asked for six grid columns, so a sections slot could not be shrunk below half a section. The minimum is now four columns. In a narrow slot the DWD map moves above the warning text and takes the full width, instead of squeezing the headline to one letter per line. Wider cards look as before.
- **Long headlines wrap inside the card.** A long single word such as "Trinkwasserverunreinigung" no longer overflows. In the narrowest layout the headline is hyphenated at syllables where your browser has a dictionary for your language, instead of breaking in the middle of a word.

## Fixes

- **Warning times use the server time zone when you ask for it.** With "Use server time zone" in your profile, the clock times, the weekday names and the today/tomorrow boundaries were still computed in the browser's zone. They now follow the setting, like the rest of Home Assistant.
- **A merged NINA and DWD warning shows the later end time.** The card kept the NINA end time even when the matching DWD warning ended later. It now shows the latest one.
- **Warnings with an unknown severity are no longer hidden by `hide_on_level_below`.** An unknown, missing or lowercase NINA severity counted as level 0 and was filtered out. The severity is now matched regardless of case, and a NINA warning without a recognised severity always stays visible.
- **The DWD map dropdown is filled in every language.** In the editor, languages without their own translation got an empty list of maps. They now fall back to the English names.
- **No more errors for foreign entities.** A configured prefix could match entities of other integrations, which were passed to `nina.get_details` and logged an error each. Only entities of the NINA integration are asked now.
- **Remote images in warning text are no longer loaded.** A warning description could make the card fetch images from any website, which could track you. Only inline images and images from your own Home Assistant are kept.
- **The map, the enlarged map and "show more" work from the keyboard.** The map opens with Enter or Space, "show more" is a real button, and the enlarged map is a labelled dialog that takes focus, closes with Escape and returns focus to the map. Focus rings are visible. Before, all three reacted to the mouse only.

## Under the hood

- **Updated tooling.** Build and test dependencies are current, the Home Assistant test image is pinned, the end-to-end tests run in GitHub Actions, and a weekly canary watches core's integrations and the DWD maps. None of this ships in the card itself.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do after updating; refresh the browser cache so the new `nina-dwd-card.js` is loaded. If you use `color_overrides`, nothing changes for you. Without overrides, expect the new severity colours described above.
